i0: **Linking words** (conjunctions) join ideas: *I like tea **and** coffee. It's cheap **but** good. Tea **or** coffee? It was late, **so** I went home. I went home **because** it was late.*
i1: This page starts with the basics and goes up to formal linkers like *however* and *therefore*. For *although* and *despite*, see [Although, Despite and In Spite Of](/blog/grammar/although-despite-in-spite-of/).
abo-basic.s: ***And*** adds information. ***But*** shows a **contrast** (a different or surprising idea). ***Or*** gives a **choice**.
abo-basic.b1: You can join **words** (*bread **and** butter*) or **sentences** (*I called her, **but** she didn't answer*).
abo-basic.b2: Use ***or*** in negative sentences: *I don't like tea **or** coffee.* (not *and coffee* here)
abo-basic.b3: We often put a comma before *but* when it joins two sentences: *It was sunny**, but** it was cold.*
abo-so-because.t: So or because? Result and reason
abo-so-because.s: ***Because*** gives the **reason** (why?). ***So*** gives the **result** (what happened next?): *I was hungry, **so** I ate a sandwich. I ate a sandwich **because** I was hungry.*
abo-so-because.b0.0.0: *It was raining, **so** we stayed at home.*
abo-so-because.b0.0.1: *We stayed at home **because** it was raining.*
abo-so-because.b0.1.0: *I was tired, **so** I went to bed.*
abo-so-because.b0.1.1: *I went to bed **because** I was tired.*
abo-so-because.b1: ***Because*** can also start the sentence; then use a comma: ***Because** it was raining, we stayed at home.*
abo-so-because.b2: Don't use *so* and *because* together: *Because it was late, I went home.* (not *Because it was late, so I went home.*)
abo-because-of.t: Because or because of? So, that's why
abo-because-of.s: ***Because*** + a **clause** (subject + verb): *because **it was** raining*. ***Because of*** + a **noun**: *because of **the rain***. ***That's why*** = so (in speaking).
abo-because-of.b0.3.1: *It was raining. **That's why** we stayed in.*
abo-because-of.b1: After ***because of***, use a noun, a pronoun or *-ing*: *because of **him**, because of **the traffic***.
abo-also-too.s: ***Also*** goes **before** the main verb (after *be*): *I **also** play tennis.* ***Too*** and ***as well*** go at the **end**: *I play tennis **too / as well**.* In negatives, use ***either***: *I don't like it **either**.*
abo-also-too.b0.0.1: before the main verb, after *be* and auxiliaries
abo-also-too.b0.3.2: *She doesn't speak German, and I don't **either**.*
abo-also-too.b1: ***Also*** is more common in writing; ***too*** and ***as well*** are more common in speaking.
abo-also-too.b2: Don't use *too* in negatives: *I don't like it **either*** (not *I don't like it too*).
x.abo-so-because-b09: Don't use *because* and *so* together (or: *It was my birthday, so…*).
